Posted February 9, 2001
Special to MarijuanaNews
I was greatly saddened to learn of the latest set-back in the Todd McCormick case.
See
Todd McCormick’s Letter from The Hole: " I say that we should not fear. I'm in the heart of the monster and feel no fear. "

The federal government got a stay on Todd’s appeal until the Supreme Court rules on the Oakland Cannabis Buyer's Club case. The Court is expected to hear that case in late March and rule in June or July of this year. This also means that there can be no release on an appeal bond, until then.

The relevance of the OCBC case is that it is about the right to claim " medical necessity " as a defense. Todd and his codefendant, the late Peter McWilliams, were denied the right even to mention their medical histories, or the medical use of marijuana. That cost Peter his life and Todd his freedom.

An adverse ruling would presumably leave Todd without any further basis for an appeal, and he would have to serve the full 5 years, or until we get the laws changed, whichever comes first.

I talked with Todd this afternoon, and he is doing as well as can be expected. We hope to interview him on the 420 MarijuanaNews on Pot-TV on Monday.

There is nothing that most people can do about the OCBC case, but everyone can do something to hasten the end of marijuana prohibition. Certainly everyone can write Todd and other drug war prisoners to try and cheer them up.

We must never forget them. We must never let them think that we have forgotten them.

Please send Todd encouraging mail at:
Todd Patrick McCormick
